title: Prepare work sites for insecticide, herbicide and fungicide interventions

lessons.title: Preparing people, premises and the client
lessons.html:
Why preparation matters

Most problems during spray treatments come from poor preparation: food left out, people walking into wet spray, pets in the treated room, drift onto a vegetable garden, or a borehole contaminated during mixing. Careful preparation protects people and makes the treatment work better.

Before the day

  • Confirm the work plan, treatment areas, products and timing with the client.
  • Give the client written preparation instructions, for example: clean kitchen surfaces, empty cupboards, cover or remove food and utensils, remove pets, birds and fish tanks or cover and switch off aquarium pumps as the label requires, and arrange for vulnerable people to be away.
  • For outdoor herbicide or fungicide work, identify neighbouring crops, gardens, beehives, water and sensitive areas.
  • Check the weather forecast for wind and rain.

On arrival

  1. Meet the client contact and walk through the treatment area.
  2. Check that client preparation has been done. If it has not, do not start until it is corrected, or reschedule.
  3. Confirm that occupants, workers and animals are out of the area and will stay out for the re-entry period.
  4. Identify and protect items that must not be contaminated: food, food contact surfaces, medicines, toys, animal feed and water troughs, seed, and electronic equipment.
  5. Switch off fans and air conditioning where drift into other areas is possible, if the client allows.

Notices and barriers

Place warning notices at entrances to treated areas, stating the treatment, date and time and when re-entry is allowed. Use barrier tape or cones around outdoor treatment areas such as sports fields, pavements and parking areas. Inform security and reception so they can redirect people.

Outdoor site checks

  • Measure or estimate wind speed and direction; postpone if conditions could cause drift the label warns against.
  • Do not treat if rain is expected within the period the label requires to be dry.
  • Mark buffer zones around water, beehives and sensitive crops.

lessons.title: Preparing products, equipment and the team
lessons.html:
Setting up a safe mixing area

Mixing concentrates is the highest-exposure step. Choose the mixing site with care:

  • Away from water sources, drains, boreholes and wells, and away from food areas and people.
  • On a level, impermeable surface or a drip tray, with a spill kit at hand.
  • Where clean water is available for mixing and for emergency washing.
  • With good ventilation if indoors.

Preparing the products

  1. Bring only the products needed, in original labelled containers.
  2. Read the label again: target, rate, mixing order, PPE, precautions, re-entry period.
  3. Calculate the amount of product and water using your calibration data.
  4. Measure with dedicated measuring jugs and scales.
  5. Fill the tank partly with water, add product as the label directs, then top up and agitate.
  6. Triple rinse empty containers into the spray tank where the label allows, and secure them for disposal.
  7. Never leave mixed product or concentrates unattended.

Preparing equipment

  • Check that sprayers, nozzles, hoses and seals are clean, undamaged and calibrated.
  • Fit the correct nozzle for the treatment: pin-stream for crack and crevice, fan for surfaces and weeds, low-drift nozzles near sensitive areas.
  • Test with clean water before adding product.
  • Use dedicated equipment for herbicides where possible.

Preparing the team

Hold a short toolbox talk. Cover the treatment areas and boundaries, products and their hazards, PPE, who does what, communication, and emergency procedures including the location of the first aid kit, emergency water and the label and SDS for the doctor. Confirm everyone wears the PPE the label specifies and that respirator cartridges are in date.

Final pre-start check

CheckDone?
Area clear of people and animalsYes / No
Food and sensitive items protectedYes / No
Notices and barriers in placeYes / No
Weather suitableYes / No
Mix correct, equipment working, PPE onYes / No

Key points

  • Give the client written preparation instructions and check they were followed before starting.
  • Clear the area of people and animals and protect food, water and sensitive items.
  • Post notices and barriers and check wind and rain before outdoor work.
  • Mix on an impermeable surface away from water, following the label and calibration data.
  • Brief the team and confirm PPE before any product is applied.
